summary.headline: Banswara Syntex Q1 FY27 total income rose 4.1% to INR322.4 crores with PAT of INR4.4 crores versus a loss of INR1.4 crores; management reiterates FY27 revenue of INR1,450–1,500 crores.
summary.overview: Total income grew 4.1% YoY to INR322.4 crores and EBITDA was INR29.5 crores (about 9% margin), with PAT of INR4.4 crores against a loss a year earlier. Fabric grew 25% YoY while yarn and garment revenues fell, mainly on labour shortages in spinning, higher internal yarn consumption and garment dispatches delayed by West Asia logistics. Management kept FY27 guidance of about INR1,500 crores revenue and 12% EBITDA, relying on a garment order book booked through November/December and a recovery in H2. Analysts pressed hard on the low top-line growth over a decade and on the pace of garment capacity additions.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Revenue INR96 crores (vs INR110 crores YoY); sales volume 36 lakh kg at 70% capacity utilisation. Higher internal transfers to fabric and garments reduced external sales; labour shortage cut output.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Revenue INR147 crores (+25% YoY); volume 59 lakh meters (+18% YoY) at 80% utilisation. Growth driven by value-added bi-stretch and wool blends; Q1 margin was in line with the 12–14% target. Roughly 50:50 export and domestic.

segments.name: Garment
segments.commentary: Revenue INR69 crores (vs INR75 crores YoY); 8 lakh pieces at 69% utilisation. West Asia logistics delayed dispatches; margin below target (8–10% expected) due to container availability. About 60% export, 40% domestic.

segments.name: Jackets (within garment)
segments.commentary: Q1 closed at about 135,000 jackets, soft demand. Run rate now upwards of 75,000 a month; FY27 target 800,000–900,000 jackets versus about 600,000 a year on average.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of about INR1,450–1,500 crores maintained; management expects garment at about INR100 crores per quarter for the next three quarters and about INR375–380 crores for the year plus export incentives.
Consolidated EBITDA target of about 12% for FY27 versus 9% in Q1; segment targets: fabric 12–14%, garment 8–10%, yarn 8–10%.
Yarn expected to normalise progressively as labour availability improves; management expects visible improvement from Q2.
Surat facility targeted for DTA use by November/December 2026 and operations from April 2027; main impact in FY28. Restart seen adding about INR200 crores of runway for about INR50 crores investment.
Garment EU operationalisation with Mango, Celio and C&A targeted by end-December 2026/early January 2027.
capex_capacity: Capex of about INR140 crores planned and sanctioned for this year across fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
Management targets about 20–25% garment expansion and about 20% fabric expansion in FY28, with a further 20% in FY28 as stated; yarn to be maintained or marginally grown.
Over the last three years, about INR350 crores invested: about INR150 crores in fabric and about INR130 crores in yarn; management said the modernisation phase is complete.
Surat facility shut to move into DTA; Daman capacity to be fully utilised this year.
demand_pricing: Garment order book fully booked through November and into December; fabric order book shows orders up to November end.
Demand healthy in US and domestic markets; Europe and Middle East softer in fabric.
India-UK FTA effective 15 July 2026; UK fabric exposure about INR70–80 crores a year; UK garment about INR20–25 crores, targeted to double to at least INR50 crores next year.
Two EU anchor garment customers (Mango and Celio) about INR100 crores of revenue; C&A onboarded with trial orders; new UK customers Haggar and NEXT added in fabric.
Domestic yarn realisations improved, partly offsetting lower volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export contribution for fabric and garments, and what are the jacket volumes and segment margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall exports 48%; fabric and garment together about 70% of export turnover. Jackets: about 600,000 a year average, FY27 expected 800,000–900,000. Segment margin targets given (fabric 12–14%, garment and yarn 8–10%).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the sequential drop so sharp in garment and yarn, and is the garment shortfall shipment timing or lost demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to a weak autumn/winter export season and seasonal domestic lull, plus delayed shipments. July garment sales were on target at about INR30 crores, with quarterly run-rate expected to reach about INR100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 12% EBITDA for FY27 on INR1,500 crores revenue; Q1 was 9%, with the rest expected to average out to 12% over the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth muted despite about INR500 crores of capex over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn capacity was under-used because of labour issues and the investments are now expected to lift top line and bottom line; fabric growth of about 20% a year is expected from its investments.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company different this decade, given flat revenue since FY19 and weak margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the dissolution of the French JV for lost sales a decade ago, said product mix is much better, and cited import substitution of Chinese goods and FTAs. Garment export share rose from about 20% to about 60%, with a target of 70%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any update on the Surat facility?
qa_highlights.answer: GIDC approvals and no-objection certificate received; customs duty clearance and SEZ debonding pending, expected within 3–5 months. Restart would involve fresh machinery, adding about INR200 crores of capacity for about INR50 crores.

risks_watch: Garment margin recovery (targeted 8–10%) depends on export mix and on timely container availability; Q1 garment EBITDA fell short.
Yarn utilisation (70% in Q1) depends on labour availability; labour shortages recur each festival and marriage season.
FY27 guidance needs about INR1,000 crores or more of revenue in Q2–Q4 at the stated quarterly run rate, with H2 weighted delivery.
Europe and Middle East fabric demand softer; West Asia logistics disruptions continue to delay shipments.
Surat restart timelines (DTA by Nov/Dec 2026, operations April 2027) and capex of about INR140 crores; benefits seen mainly in FY28.
Debt rising to about INR500 crores per analyst estimate; past capex has not yet translated into revenue growth.

key_quotes: Our order book continues to be robust and is fully booked through to November and even December now, providing us with strong revenue visibility and confidence for the coming quarters.
So imagine if the yarn utilization goes up to 90%, you will have a really good top line and bottom line both happening.
We hope to recover the rest in the 3 quarters that are to come to average out 12%. We are still maintaining that.
So we are looking at closing close to about INR400 crores this year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 guidance, with the order book (garments booked to November/December) as the main support. Cautious and somewhat defensive on the sharp Q1 shortfall, which management attributed to labour shortages, shipment delays and a weak autumn/winter export season, and on the decade of flat revenue.
